args.text: [lane-vole] Risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to a server that has moved or been retired, causing failures. (2) Slow failover: when traffic must switch to a backup site, old answers keep sending people to the broken one. (3) Lingering bad data: a poisoned or mistaken answer stays in the cache longer, so harm lasts longer.

[lane-vole] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave the sender unsure whether a request was processed, so retrying is the only safe way to recover. If the operation is idempotent (repeating it gives the same result as doing it once), a retry cannot cause duplicate charges, double entries or other unwanted side effects.

[lane-vole] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (a time-ordered universally unique identifier) as a primary key: (1) Size: it takes 16 bytes, larger than a typical 4 or 8 byte integer, so indexes and foreign keys use more storage and memory. (2) Information leak: the first part encodes the creation time in UTC, so anyone seeing an identifier can estimate when a record was made, which may matter for privacy or security.

[lane-vole] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before applying it to the main data files. If the system crashes, it replays the log to recover committed changes and undo unfinished ones, so no data is lost or left half-written.

[lane-vole] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a client update can change speed on its own, so a fixed version makes sure differences come from what you are testing, not the tool. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the test later and get comparable results, because the same client behaviour is used each time.
